cmd: browser-pilot do "Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in the browser. If a login form appears, sign in with username '«redacted»' and password '«redacted»' (if Grafana asks you to change the password, skip that step). Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (try the search/dashboards browse). Once it is open, report the exact titles of all the panels on that dashboard, exactly as displayed on the page." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000, create a NEW dashboard (Dashboards -> New dashboard -> Add visualization). For the data source choose the 'TestData DB' data source (it may be listed as 'TestData DB' or 'TestData'; do NOT use the default Grafana testdata if it is named differently - pick the TestData one). Change the panel visualization type to 'Stat'. Set the panel title to exactly 'bgr3 Availability'. Then save the dashboard with the title exactly 'bgr3 Bench Dashboard' (Save dashboard dialog: name it 'bgr3 Bench Dashboard', leave folder as General, and save). After saving, report the dashboard's URL/UID and confirm the panel title and visualization type shown on the page." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open the dashboard with UID ffw6ame4shr7ka (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/new-dashboard). Open the dashboard settings (gear icon / 'Dashboard settings') and go to the General settings page. Set the dashboard Name/title to exactly 'bgr3 Bench Dashboard'. Also add a dashboard tag with the value 'bench' (in the Tags field, type 'bench' and press Enter so it becomes a tag chip). Then click Save, and if a save dialog appears confirm saving. After saving, verify by reopening dashboard settings and report the dashboard title and the tags shown, plus the current URL." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard (exit any settings/edit view first). Add a NEW Text panel to this dashboard (use the 'Add' button -> 'Visualization', then change the visualization type to 'Text'). Set the panel title to exactly 'bgr3 Notes'. In the Text panel content editor, enter markdown text that includes the runid 'bgr3' - for example: '## bgr3 Notes\\n\\nBenchmark run bgr3 - created for the dashboard build flow test.' Make sure the text content actually contains the string 'bgr3'. Then click Save (the dashboard save button) and confirm the save dialog so the dashboard is persisted. After saving, report the panel titles visible on the dashboard and confirm the Text panel content includes 'bgr3'." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard in Grafana (make sure you are not in edit mode). Report: (1) the exact titles of every panel visible on the dashboard, (2) whether the Text panel titled 'bgr3 Notes' displays text content that contains the string 'bgr3' (quote the visible text), and (3) whether the Stat panel titled 'bgr3 Availability' is present. Do not change anything - this is read-only verification." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard and edit the Text panel titled 'bgr3 Notes' (open the panel's menu and choose Edit, or use URL parameter ?editPanel=2). In the panel editor, find the Text panel content editor (a markdown/code editor area, currently showing placeholder text like 'Title' and 'For markdown syntax help'). Click into that content editor and type/replace its content with this exact markdown: '## bgr3 Notes\\n\\nBenchmark run bgr3 - created for the dashboard build flow test.' Make sure the editor's value actually contains the string 'bgr3' (read back the field value to confirm). Then click the 'Save dashboard' button in the top toolbar and confirm the save dialog so it persists (look for a 'Dashboard saved' message). Then navigate back to the dashboard view (not edit mode) and report the visible text content of the 'bgr3 Notes' panel." --session bgr3 --json --timeout 420

browser-pilot do "Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard in Grafana in view mode (no editPanel in URL). Report the visible text content of the Text panel titled 'bgr3 Notes' (quote it exactly), and state whether it contains the string 'bgr3'. Also report the titles of all panels on the dashboard. Read-only - do not change anything." --session bgr3 --json

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard?editPanel=2 to edit the Text panel 'bgr3 Notes'. The panel's Content field is a Monaco code editor. IMPORTANT: do NOT use JavaScript/monaco API or fill() to set the value - that does not work. Instead: (a) click directly into the middle of the Monaco editor text area to focus it and place the cursor, (b) press Control+A (or Meta+A) to select all existing text, (c) then TYPE the following text using real keyboard input: ## bgr3 Notes  then press Enter twice, then type: Benchmark run bgr3 - created for the dashboard build flow test.  After typing, verify the editor now shows that text. Then click 'Save dashboard' in the top toolbar and confirm any save dialog, and wait for the 'Dashboard saved' confirmation. Finally navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard (view mode) and report the exact visible text of the 'bgr3 Notes' panel and whether it contains 'bgr3'." --session bgr3 --json --timeout 420

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard in view mode. Two tasks, then one save: (1) Click the time range picker in the top toolbar (it shows something like 'Last 6 hours' or 'Last 24 hours') and set the absolute/relative range to 'Last 6 hours' (choose it from the quick ranges list). (2) Click the auto-refresh / refresh interval picker (the dropdown next to the refresh button, often showing 'Off' or a time like '5m') and set the auto-refresh interval to '1m'. (3) Then click 'Save dashboard' in the top toolbar and confirm the save dialog so these settings persist - wait for the 'Dashboard saved' message. IMPORTANT: the save must happen AFTER setting both the time range and the refresh interval. After saving, reload the page fresh (navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard) and report: the time range shown in the top toolbar, and the auto-refresh interval shown in the refresh dropdown." --session bgr3 --json --timeout 420

browser-pilot do "In Grafana, open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard and open Dashboard settings (gear icon), then go to the 'JSON Model' page. The JSON model is shown in a Monaco editor. I need the dashboard JSON to contain a top-level property \\\"refresh\\\": \\\"1m\\\" (and keep the existing \\\"time\\\" range of now-6h to now). The JSON editor is a Monaco editor - to edit it: click into the editor, press Control+A to select all, then use real keyboard typing is too error-prone for a large JSON. Instead, a better approach: click the 'Copy' or use the editor, but the most reliable way is: click into the Monaco editor, press Control+A, then press Delete to clear it, then type the full corrected JSON? That is too long. ALTERNATIVE PREFERRED APPROACH: instead of editing JSON by hand, go back to the dashboard, enter edit mode (click 'Edit' / the pencil), and in edit mode use the top toolbar's refresh-interval dropdown (next to the refresh icon) to select '1m', THEN click 'Save dashboard' and confirm. If the refresh dropdown is not visible in edit mode, try setting it in view mode first (URL gets ?refresh=1m), then enter edit mode WITHOUT reloading (the refresh setting should carry over), then Save dashboard and confirm. After saving, reload the page fresh at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard and report what the refresh interval dropdown shows." --session bgr3 --json --timeout 420

browser-pilot do "Final read-only verification in Grafana. Do NOT change anything. Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffw6ame4shr7ka/bgr3-bench-dashboard fresh (view mode, no editPanel, no editview params). Report all of the following from the page: (1) the dashboard title shown in the page header/breadcrumb, (2) the exact titles of every panel on the dashboard, (3) the visible text content of the Text panel titled 'bgr3 Notes' and whether it contains 'bgr3', (4) the visualization type of the panel titled 'bgr3 Availability' - to check this, open that panel's menu and choose Edit, look at the visualization selector at the top of the panel editor to confirm it says 'Stat', and also report which data source is selected in the query editor for that panel, then press Escape/Back to exit edit mode WITHOUT saving, (5) the time range shown in the top toolbar, (6) the auto-refresh interval shown in the refresh dropdown next to the refresh button, (7) the dashboard tags - open Dashboard settings (gear) -> General and report the tags shown, then close settings without saving. Report each item with the exact value observed." --session bgr3 --json --timeout 420
